summary:
Set 119 Session 3 (SET-TERMINAL) restores the backstop's recovery path, stops a close-mandated write from staling the verdict it just earned, and deletes what nothing reaches -- after proving unreachability rather than assuming it.

(1) CLOSE-MANDATED WRITES ARE NOW A DECLARED CATEGORY. The constitution MANDATES `cite_lessons` in the final commit, and its `last-used-set` bump staled the verification stamp between verifying and closing -- so citing sessions were plausibly buying a routed round for a metadata trailer, invisibly, because the backstop simply re-verified and re-stamped. The freshness exclusions had an unstated PER-SET scope and no concept of a close-mandated write outside it. Adding two filenames would have fixed the instance and left the class alive for the third time (L-069-1). So a writer now DECLARES a module-level `CLOSE_MANDATED_WRITES` literal and `verification_stamp` DISCOVERS it by parsing the source with `ast` -- no import, no side effects, safe on the close path. A fifth close-mandated writer is exempt the moment it says so, in EITHER scope, with no list here to edit. The `bound` field carries the honesty: a per-set ledger is close output end to end (`whole-file`), but a guidance file is only PARTLY close output -- the close owns one trailer field and the lesson prose around it is session WORK. Exempting the file wholesale would have let a post-verification rewrite of a PRELOAD document ride a passed round, which is a verification reduction and therefore not this session's to make. `cite_lessons` declares a normalizer instead, and the digest compares normalized-current against normalized-at-base, dropping the file only when the mandated field alone moved.

(2) THE BACKSTOP'S OWN RECOVERY PATH WORKS. Its blocking message said 're-verify with verify_session', but `--phase remediation-review` failed closed with EXIT_USAGE unless a prior round had recorded a `discoveryBaselineTree` -- and the envelope that carried it is written ONLY on a findings-bearing round, so the two states that most needed a baseline left none: a CLEAN discovery round, and EVERY close-backstop round (which is unphased). `record_round_completed` now takes an omit-null `discovery_baseline_tree` and `find_discovery_baseline_tree` reads the ledger as well as the envelopes; the ledger has no findings precondition. The ENVELOPE field kept its Set 096 meaning exactly (discovery-family only) -- the full pytest run caught the first cut widening it, and the fix narrowed the change to the ledger where it belonged. A remediation-review round is excluded from recording a baseline on purpose, or a second cycle would diff from the first fix instead of from the original discovery baseline. The refusal message now names `--phase remediation-review`, and a test PARSES that message and executes the command it names from the exact state it was printed in.

(3) AN OVERSIZED BUNDLE NO LONGER TAKES THE GATE DOWN. `EvidenceTooLargeError` and `VerifySessionError` were siblings; `close_backstop` catches the parent at four sites and caught the sibling at exactly one, so an oversized evidence bundle crashed the close with an unhandled traceback on four paths -- the gate gone, no remediation line, on the most expensive path there is. Making it a SUBCLASS fixes all four by type. The exit-code split never lived in the class relationship, only in handler ORDER, and the `verify_session` CLI caught the parent FIRST -- so the reorder was mandatory, not cosmetic: a subclass caught after its parent is unreachable code, and without it the fail-closed verification-unavailable exit would have silently downgraded to a usage error.

(4) FOUR MODULES NOTHING REACHED ARE GONE, AND THE SPEC'S LIST WAS WRONG ABOUT THREE. Unreachability was PROVEN FIRST with a static import graph over all 78 `ai_router` modules (ast, no execution) against the spec's three criteria. Deleted: `floor_ratchet` (914), `routed_gate` (437), `pricing_proposal` (1,581), `cost_report` (551) = 3,483 module LOC plus 3,012 lines of tests (235 tests). KEPT AND REPORTED, because the proof says they are reached: `contract_gate` (`close_session.run` calls `validate_contract_gate` as a live close gate), `spec_admission` (`session_checklist` calls `parse_session_plans` to seed the plan the `checklist_posted` gate reads), and `replacement_gate` (`dual_surface_verify` imports and calls `validate_benchmark_registration`). The line, journaled: a module is reachable when a SURVIVING module CALLS it, and an `__init__` re-export is publication, not use. Nothing was edited to manufacture unreachability -- that is the 'forcing' the spec forbids. THE SPEC'S 'Ends with' FIGURE OF 5,165 LINES IS THEREFORE WRONG, and this session reports it rather than quietly meeting a smaller number.

Verification: ONE round, VERIFIED, zero findings across both discovery lenses (spec-conformance and failure-scenario), cross-provider to gpt-5.5 with anthropic excluded.

notes.set_terminal: Final session of Set 119. change-log.md is authored here. `pathAwareCritique` is deliberately absent from this set's configuration, so no critique artifact is owed. Nothing is published: pyproject.toml stays at 1.0.0 and all three Set 119 changelog sections remain [Unreleased]; the version bump belongs to the release walk. No extension change -- nothing here touches tools/.
notes.verification_loop: ONE round. `--phase discovery` with the configured 2-call fan-out (lenses: spec-conformance, failure-scenario), both answered by gpt-5.5 with the orchestrator's effective provider (anthropic, via model-registry lookup on claude-opus-5) excluded. Verdict VERIFIED, 0 blocking, 0 minor/nit -- so there is no adjudicated-minor residual and nothing was disputed, dismissed or waived. Cost recorded as $0.00: this is a Copilot CLI seat, where billed usage is unavailable by design. An up-front conventions block (s3-conventions.md) stated the suite baseline, the release contract, the five by-design exclusions and the consequence rubric, per L-064-10.
notes.test_run_of_record: pytest: 3,780 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed in 513.23s (8:33), run on the frozen tree AFTER the last code change and recorded in test-runs.jsonl (digest 859283c79f4f, 514s). The suite is 235 tests smaller than before this session, entirely because four test modules were deleted with the four modules they covered; no test was weakened, disabled or made lenient. An earlier full run FAILED one test (test_verify_session_phases.py::test_no_phase_envelope_carries_no_phase_fields) and it was a real finding, not a flake: the first cut of the baseline change had widened the Set 096 ENVELOPE contract when only the round LEDGER needed widening. The fix narrowed the change; the suite was then re-run in full so the run of record postdates the last code change.
notes.spec_discrepancy_reported: The spec's Session 3 'Ends with' line promises '5,165 lines nothing reaches are gone' and its step 4 names five gate modules as unreachable from any close path. Measured: three of the seven listed modules are REACHED and were kept. contract_gate is called by close_session.run (a live close gate), close_preflight and start_session; spec_admission is called by session_checklist to seed the step plan the checklist_posted gate reads; replacement_gate is imported at module scope and called by dual_surface_verify. Deleting them would have required editing surviving modules to manufacture unreachability, which the spec's own deletion rule forbids ('a module that turns out to be reachable stays and is reported, not forced'). The measured deletion is 3,483 module LOC + 3,012 test LOC across four modules. This is a finding about the SPEC's prediction, stated here rather than silently met.
decisions_this_session: Deletion scope (authority=ai, rubric_line=goal-over-letter, verification_effect=none): delete four, keep three, report the discrepancy. The criterion drawn and journaled -- a module is reachable when a surviving module CALLS it; an __init__ re-export is publication, not use -- is what separates routed_gate/cost_report (deleted) from replacement_gate (kept).

Normalizer over whole-file exemption for the guidance files (implicit in the category design, recorded in the code comments and the changelog): a whole-file exemption would have been simpler and would have reduced verification, by letting a post-verification rewrite of an always-loaded preload document ride a passed round. The normalizer reduces nothing.
notes.residuals_taken_from_session_2: Two of the four residuals Session 2 handed over were taken as the spec directed: the cite_lessons stamp staleness (step 2) and the EvidenceTooLargeError sibling sites (step 3c). Two remain DEFERRED by the spec's own decision and are re-recorded below.
owed_residuals: The doc-only cap's blast radius is still unmeasured. Named by Session 1, not folded in by Session 2 (the replay reads session-events.jsonl -- close-out failures -- while this question needs sN-issues*.json, a different corpus and a different instrument), and deferred by this session's spec because a sixth step doubles the median session length (Set 111 S4). Still owed.

close_preflight reports 'would-refuse' for an already-closed session. close_session.run checks _is_already_closed and returns noop_already_closed (exit 0) BEFORE any gate runs; the preflight walks the chain regardless. Deferred on purpose by this session's spec: low consequence, and it would drag close_preflight.py into a session that otherwise does not touch it. The fix is a few lines at the top of `evaluate` plus a falsifier pair.

evidencePaths is contract but unenforced -- nothing refuses a blocking finding that omits it, because refusing would make an uncited finding CHEAPER to raise. If enforcement is ever wanted, the honest form is a report, not a gate. (Session 1's residual, unchanged.)

BEHAVIOURAL_MARKDOWN_PREFIXES is still a one-entry list. A second entry would signal the extension-based rule is being asked to carry a judgment it cannot; simplify the rule rather than lengthen the list. Review, not growth. (Session 1's residual, unchanged.)

EvidenceTooLargeError remains the one pre-metered backstop refusal close_preflight does not predict: it is raised by evidence assembly AFTER decide_backstop returns, and assembling evidence on every preflight run would make a run-it-on-a-whim tool no longer cheap. Step 3c made the resulting failure SURVIVABLE (a gate outcome with a remediation line instead of a traceback) rather than predictable, which was the affordable half.
notes.next_set_recommendation: The preload collapse (session-constitution.md / project-guidance.md / lessons-learned.md into executable code and one-line instructions) is the natural successor and the spec names it: it depended on Session 1's doc-only cap landing first, because preload wording churn is precisely what the cap keeps out of the metered loop. The constitution sits at 3,984 of its 4,000-token ceiling and ceilings ratchet down only, so that set opens with an eviction decision. Set 117 remains in progress (Sessions 2-3 pending) and owns pytest.ini, the Playwright worker policy and scripts/vscode-launch.js; this set touched none of them.
